name: Liber abaci positional arithmetic
summary: Fibonacci's revised Liber abaci taught Italian readers to write numbers with nine figures and 0 by place value, with worked examples of arithmetic.
description: The revised Liber abaci teaches writing numbers with nine figures plus 0, decimal place values and explicit empty-place examples such as 209, alongside arithmetic procedures.
tier_reason: Retain the mathematical synthesis; the surviving Siena copy cannot automatically displace1202/1228 composition evidence. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.
why: Leonardo learned Arabic-Indian reckoning while with his merchant father in North Africa and wrote it up for Italian commercial use.

date.label: 1228 revision
date.basis: Dates the surviving revised work, not the lost first redaction of 1202 or the date of its later manuscript copies.

date.label: Late 13th to early 14th century (estimated)
date.basis: Devlin estimates late 13th century; Germano identifies the manuscript as late 13th to early 14th century. The half-century endpoints encode a broad approximate reading, not proven limits.

events.statement: A Siena manuscript preserves the first page of the revised Liber abaci, including its numeral teaching.
events.caveats: Devlin says late 13th century; Germano extends the estimate into the early 14th century. The half-century endpoints are conventional estimates, not secure dating limits. Current Siena custody does not establish where it was copied; copying does not prove arithmetic use.

links.statement: Leonardo links his instruction at Bugia and later study of Indian calculation methods to his decision to compose Liber abaci; its revised text explicitly teaches positional numerals and zero.
links.scope: Bugia and later Mediterranean study to the Latin Liber abaci; childhood instruction before the composition dated 1202, surviving revision 1228.
links.alternatives: Twelfth-century Latin algorisms provided other routes independent of this autobiographical episode.
links.caveats: The relation relies on Leonardo's account. No al-Khwarizmi book, particular teacher or complete chain from India is identified.
links.timing: Instruction precedes initial composition; content is shown at the surviving revision's date to avoid backdating details.
